title: Grilled Turmeric Chicken Satay with Peanut Sauce & Cucumber Salad
dek: Golden, lightly charred chicken skewers pair with a warm chile-peanut sauce and a crisp cucumber-red onion salad for a practical Southeast Asian-inspired dinner.
image_alt: Golden grilled turmeric chicken satay skewers beside brown peanut sauce and cucumber-red onion salad
ingredients: 12 flat bamboo skewers, 8 to 10 inches long, soaked in water 30 minutes, or 12 metal skewers
1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, trimmed and cut lengthwise into strips about 1 inch wide
1 1/4 cups unsweetened full-fat coconut milk, stirred well and divided
2 tbsp packed light brown sugar, divided
1 tbsp neutral high-heat oil, plus more for the grill grates
2 tsp finely grated fresh ginger, divided
2 to 4 tbsp hot water, as needed
1/4 medium red onion, very thinly sliced (about 1/2 cup)

instructions.name: Soak the skewers and make the marinade
instructions.text: Cover bamboo skewers with water and weigh them down for 30 minutes; skip this step for metal skewers. In a medium bowl, whisk 1/2 cup coconut milk, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, the fish sauce, 1 tablespoon brown sugar, the oil, 2 grated garlic cloves, 1 teaspoon ginger, turmeric, coriander and black pepper.

instructions.name: Marinate the chicken safely
instructions.text: Add the chicken strips to the marinade and turn until every surface is yellow and evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes or up to 8 hours. Keep this raw-chicken marinade separate from the peanut sauce and discard it after threading; do not use it as a baste.

instructions.name: Quick-pickle the cucumber salad
instructions.text: While the chicken marinates, whisk the rice vinegar, 1 tablespoon water, remaining 1 tablespoon brown sugar, 1 tablespoon lime juice and the salt in a shallow bowl. Add the cucumbers and red onion, toss well and refrigerate. Toss once more before serving so the crisp vegetables stay visibly dressed but not submerged.

instructions.name: Simmer the peanut sauce
instructions.text: In a small saucepan, whisk the peanut butter, 3/4 cup coconut milk, remaining 2 tablespoons soy sauce, red curry paste, remaining garlic clove, remaining 1 teaspoon ginger and remaining 1 tablespoon lime juice. Cook over medium-low heat for 3 to 5 minutes, whisking, until glossy and gently steaming. Thin with hot water 1 tablespoon at a time until it pours slowly from a spoon; keep warm without boiling.

instructions.name: Thread flat, even skewers
instructions.text: Heat a gas or charcoal grill to medium-high, about 425 to 450°F at the grates. Remove the chicken from the marinade and let excess drip back into the bowl. Thread each strip onto a skewer in a loose accordion, keeping the meat in a single flat layer; divide the chicken evenly among 12 skewers. Discard the used marinade.

instructions.name: Grill to a golden char and 165°F
instructions.text: Clean and lightly oil the hot grates. Grill the skewers in an uncrowded layer for 3 to 4 minutes per side, closing the lid between turns, until the edges are lightly charred. Check the thickest folded section on several skewers with a clean instant-read thermometer; every piece must reach 165°F. Transfer cooked skewers to a clean platter, never the raw-chicken tray.

instructions.name: Plate to match the finished dish
instructions.text: Arrange three golden skewers per person. Spoon the warm brown peanut sauce into a wide shallow bowl for dipping and serve the drained cucumber-red onion salad separately, matching the visible components in the photograph. Serve immediately while the chicken is hot and the salad is crisp.

why_it_works: Coconut milk carries turmeric, coriander, garlic and ginger across the chicken while its fat protects the thin strips from drying on the grill.
Flat accordion folds expose more surface to direct heat than compact cubes, producing the browned edges shown in the photograph while still cooking quickly to 165°F.
Natural peanut butter and coconut milk create a cohesive sauce, while lime and red curry paste cut through its richness without hiding the roasted-peanut flavor.
A brief vinegar pickle keeps cucumber and red onion crisp and sharp, giving the rich skewers and sauce a cool counterpoint.
Making the sauce in its own saucepan avoids cross-contamination from the raw-chicken marinade and lets its consistency be adjusted precisely with hot water.
swaps: Use boneless skinless chicken breast in the same weight, slicing it across the grain into 1-inch-wide strips. Begin checking at 5 minutes total because breast meat dries faster than thighs.
For a fish-sauce-free version, replace the fish sauce with 2 teaspoons additional soy sauce. The flavor will be less briny but the marinade will still season the chicken.
Use sunflower-seed butter for a peanut-free sauce and verify the curry paste, soy sauce and seed butter are produced without peanut cross-contact.
For gluten-free satay, use certified gluten-free tamari instead of soy sauce and check the fish sauce, curry paste and peanut butter labels.
No outdoor grill is required: cook the skewers in batches on a lightly oiled cast-iron grill pan over medium-high heat, using the same 165°F doneness test.
storage: Refrigerate cooked chicken skewers, peanut sauce and drained salad in separate airtight containers within 2 hours. Keep the chicken and sauce up to 4 days; the salad is best within 2 days. Reheat chicken on a covered sheet pan in a 350°F oven for 8 to 10 minutes and the sauce in a small saucepan with a splash of water, bringing both to 165°F. Freeze cooked chicken off the skewers for up to 2 months; do not freeze the cucumber salad.
notes: Natural peanut butter can separate in the jar. Stir it completely smooth before measuring so the sauce does not develop oily pockets.
Red curry paste brands vary in heat, salt and allergen content. Start with 2 teaspoons for a milder sauce, then add the final teaspoon after tasting.
If the chicken sticks, it is not ready to turn. Give it another 30 seconds so browned proteins release naturally from clean, preheated, oiled grates.
Bamboo tips can still darken even after soaking. Keep the bare ends over a cooler grill zone or place a folded strip of foil beneath them; never leave the grill unattended.
Calories and cost include three skewers, one quarter of the peanut sauce and salad per serving; actual values vary with chicken trimming, sauce consumption and local prices.

faqs.q: Can I marinate chicken satay overnight?
faqs.a: Yes. Cover and refrigerate the chicken at 40°F or below for up to 8 hours. Longer marinating is unnecessary for thin strips and can make their surface soft. Thread the skewers shortly before grilling and discard the raw marinade.

faqs.q: Why did my peanut sauce become too thick or split?
faqs.a: High heat and rapid boiling can tighten or separate peanut sauce. Keep it at medium-low, whisk continuously and add hot water 1 tablespoon at a time. If it looks oily, remove it from the heat and whisk in another spoonful of warm coconut milk or water.

faqs.q: How do I know thin chicken skewers are safely cooked?
faqs.a: Color and grill marks are not reliable. Insert a clean instant-read thermometer sideways into the thickest folded section on several skewers. Each must reach 165°F; check more than one because strip thickness and grill hot spots vary.
